changes: All seventeen existing FRED requests are retained: DFF five observations, SOFR/IORB/T10Y2Y/T5YIFR five each, DTWEXBGS sixty, and eleven nominal Treasury series ninety each. No new queries or cadence changes.

Complete accepted response bytes, parsed provider roots, original row positions, sanitized request identities, acquisition/read clocks and transport-cache provenance are retained. Failed and unrequested series remain distinct. Every row remains inspectable even when unavailable for arithmetic.

DFF selects the latest actual date without skipping a missing latest print; booleans, nonfinite strings, duplicate/future dates and observations older than five calendar days cannot become the policy context. Benchmark normalization explicitly records missing row exclusions and rejects duplicate/future dates before dictionary conversion.

Content-addressed public originals use conditional writes and bounded read/decompression checks, including conflict readback. The existing source-evidence.v1 metadata is preserved, and a mixed-writer test proves the shared writer can reuse these exact objects without losing the first acquisition time. Exact source-selection compilers, complete normalized measurements and a typed run manifest are frozen; reviewed local code replays every accepted original and compares all native policy/cross/benchmark inputs before publication.

Source capture coverage and measurement availability are separate. Zero accepted sources never claim original-byte replay. No Calls, forecast, sizing or execution qualification is enabled. The ordinary archive failure path publishes an explicit unavailable block without a stale success pointer.

A common epoch clock conversion prevents microsecond differences between OS clock APIs from inventing a future adapter read. The existing native-entry benchmark cache reset and original acquisition-aware transport cache remain.

An offline bounded-file replay command accepts the manifest reference and refuses unrelated/private paths, altered compilers, rehashed hostile references, changed outputs and compressed corruption. It never executes retained source code.
limitations: This archives effective accepted responses, not every failed HTTP attempt. The fixed existing seventeen-query universe and observation limits are explicit, not complete provider history.

Original observation definitions, provider release calendars, first-release availability and historical vintages remain unverified. Acquisition metadata is recorded by the reviewed adapter, not a signed provider attestation.

Native input selections and descriptive cross arithmetic replay. The complete legacy auction score, historical analogs, issuance model, benchmark-to-auction calculations and predictive/sizing validity are not granted by this archive.
Deployment package and static verification do not prove ordinary publication or peak native resource capacity. The original 13:05 UTC/19:50 UTC schedules remain; no manual native run is requested.
The existing page renderer remains unchanged. A dedicated FRED archive inspection interface and broader platform workstreams remain open.
